answer.rationale: The binding constraints narrow the field before memory is even consulted: the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms (memory_c4) is foreclosed this cycle; the contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, so defer_decision (memory_c5) means an actual supply lapse rather than a month-to-month glide; and renew_incumbent (memory_c1, memory_c6) is stable but cannot deliver an 18% cut at a refused price. That leaves the low-cost vendor as the only path that meets the mandate, which makes memory_c2 the single load-bearing record in the whole inheritance — it is the only evidence that this vendor performs. So it is the one I spend verification on. What I need from the archived source is the scope of that prior switch: was it primary supply at committed volume, or a smaller share? Was the 'quick onboarding' measured against a line running at 94% with no buffer, or against slack capacity? Was it one component or many, and did accurate invoicing extend through a demand peak? Consolidated summaries strip exactly these qualifiers, and a single prior success at unknown scale does not license a full-volume cutover into a line with zero buffer. Hence the guarded scale: qualify the low-cost vendor as primary via a bridged, phased transition — short bridge or partial-volume extension with the incumbent to cover the 14-day cliff, first-article and capacity audit before shifting committed volume, and staged allocation with defined revert triggers. This deliberately sacrifices some of the immediate 18% to avoid buying the cut with delivery risk, which the objective forbids. Downstream risk is real and flagged: a cutover that fails at 94% utilization has no recovery slack, and memory_c3 shows dual sourcing is what actually absorbed a shortage here — so if the audit reveals capacity thinness, add_second_source becomes the correct next-cycle move rather than deepening a single-vendor bet. I am also aware the inherited record is uniformly success-framed with no failures logged, which is a sign of survivorship in the memory itself, not of a risk-free option set; I hold the cost estimate as unconfirmed until the source record is read.
